item.description: Ty Dieffenbach #14 of the UCLA Bruins walks off the field after the game against Wisconsin Badgers at Rose Bowl Stadium on October 17, 2026 in Pasadena, California. But despite the fire, Dieffenbach thrived. You can go play ball at the highest level. I just think it was awesome seeing all of them show out. I love all of them and I appreciate them for coming out tonight.” Big Day from Dieffenbach Things started out smoothly for Dieffenbach and the Bruins. item.title: ‘I don’t think…’ – Angel Reese refuses to give Golden State Valkyries credit for her struggles
item.description: Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images Angel Reese struggled in the latter half of her first WNBA Finals game, but she didn’t give her opponents any credit for it. The Golden State Valkyries’ stellar defence kicked in during the fourth quarter of their 68-64 win against the Atlanta Dream in Game 1 of the WNBA Finals. The team found themselves down towards the end of the game, but they held the Dream to just two made field goals in the last 10 minutes of the matchup. Angel Reese started the game on fire. She had 11 points in the first quarter. But the Valkyries completely shut her down during the entire second half. She went scoreless after the break. Despite their tough defensive pressure, though, Reese suggested that her issues had nothing to do with her opponents. Angel Reese claims she wasn’t ‘aggressive enough’ in the second half of the game Reese knows a thing or two about good defence. She was named the WNBA’s Defensive Player of the Year for 2026. The Valkyries’ Gabby Williams was her main rival for the award, but Golden State’s defensive identity goes far beyond just their star. While some players may have accepted that their rivals got the better of them during a game, Reese’s comments after the game implied that her attention was focused on her own decision-making. “I don’t think they really did anything,” Reese told the media. “That was just on me, I wasn’t aggressive enough with the ball. Just need to get the ball and get to my spots. So, definitely going to do a better job of that next game.” Reese’s answer shows her maturity. The Dream star seems focused on controlling what she can instead of worrying about what her rivals are doing. 14 points in Game 1 shows that Angel can definitely score if she is at her best and that is exactly what Atlanta fans will want to see in Game 2. item.title: Enes Kanter confirms he will attend Game 3 of the WNBA Finals and ‘take some notes’ from Angel Reese
item.description: Credit: Michael Reaves/Paras Griffin via Getty Images Enes Kanter has made his intention to attend Game 3 of the WNBA Finals at the State Farm Arena in Atlanta clear. The Golden State Valkyries and the Atlanta Dream are the last two teams standing in what’s been a whirlwind WNBA season, reaching new heights of popularity on and off the court. One reason their popularity has surged off the court is former NBA player Enes Kanter, who said he will do everything in his power to declare for the WNBA Draft and has been drawing attention away from the on-court action since July. Enes Kanter shouts out Angel Reese as he confirms plans to attend WNBA Finals Game 3 Kanter revealed on X that he will be attending Game 3 of the Finals. “I’m excited to announce that I’ll be in Atlanta on October 21st for Game 3 of the WNBA Finals!” Kanter referenced Valkyries’ star Gabby Williams as one of his biggest inspirations, while also saying he will take notes on rebounding and finishing from Angel Reese while watching her play. “As you all know, this all started with an interview featuring Gabby Williams of the Golden State Valkyries, when she said, ‘I have no problem with trans athletes playing on my team or against my team.’ Her words gave me so much hope and motivation to come out as a woman and officially declare for the WNBA Draft. I can’t wait to watch my favourite player, the woman who inspired me to become who I am today!” “Second, my favourite diva has unfortunately blocked me on social media. But that won’t stop me from showing my appreciation for the one and only Angel Reese! I can’t wait to take some notes on how to finish a layup after grabbing a rebound.” Whether he admits it or not, these comments are dripping with sarcasm, as Williams’ comments were to protect trans athletes and not for cis men to exploit the WNBA’s openness to consider trans athletes in such a manner. The last time Kanter attended a WNBA game was a clash between the Chicago Sky and the Indiana Fever, getting removed from the game and banned from attending another game by the Sky for getting into a heated interaction with guard Natasha Cloud. Kanter will likely make a political statement, already implying that the T-shirt he will wear to the game will have an emphatic message. The 34-year-old former NBA center will likely be under immense scrutiny at the game, with any infraction of the fan conduct policy likely resulting in an ejection to ensure he cannot sidetrack another WNBA game with his presence on the courtside seats. The pass was in front of Sabo, but he knocked it down with his left hand. After his initial shot attempt was blocked by a sliding defender, Sabo went top shelf to make it a 1-0 game. (Photo by Keith Birmingham/MediaNews Group/Pasadena Star-News via Getty Images) | MediaNews Group via Getty Images The Wisconsin Badgers dropped their second game of the season in a 17-7 loss to the No. 12 UCLA Bruins on Saturday, as they fell to 4-2 and 2-1 in conference play. It was a very disappointing outing for the Badgers, who had plenty of opportunities on both sides of the ball, but could not score points or get off the field on third downs. As a result, they squandered a potential chance to be in the AP Top 25 next week, and now are set to face a tough two-week slate with the No. 19 USC Trojans and the No. 17 Iowa Hawkeyes up next in season-defining games. Here are three quick takeaways from the Badgers 17-7 loss to UCLA. Coaching decisions There were moments in this game where I thought both coaches made questionable decisions, with UCLA’s trick-play interception standing out for the Bruins. But, far more often than not, in a game that was there for the taking, Luke Fickell was outcoached by Bob Chesney, making a couple of headscratching field position decisions. The first major one came on Wisconsin’s second offensive drive, as the Badgers got to a 4th & 2 at the 50-yard line following UCLA’s 16-play, 84-yard field goal drive that lasted 8:42. After a bevy of questionable penalties, the Badgers, who had initially gotten to the UCLA 43-yard line, got back to the 50-yard line for a 4th & 2 after a 23-yard catch from Jaylon Domingeaux. Wisconsin had just seen UCLA march down the field with a long, sustained drive on its defense. Regardless, though, of their confidence in the defense, it felt like a clear go-for situation, with the chance to respond and put points on the board, or at least give their offense more plays. Instead, the Badgers punted, and their defense allowed a 13-play, 91-yard touchdown drive, negating the field advantage. That wasn’t the only time Wisconsin punted in neutral or plus territory. The Badgers had a huge opportunity, facing a 1st & 10 at the UCLA 39-yard line in a 10-7 game in the third quarter after a 15-yard completion on first down and a UCLA penalty. Wisconsin had just scored a touchdown on a drive that consisted of 10 rushing plays and one pass. In a favorable situation, Jeff Grimes didn’t extend off his creativity from the previous drive in the run game, where Wisconsin was clearly clicking. Instead, Wisconsin threw an incompletion on first down, got nothing on a Colton Joseph-designed run up the middle, and had an incompletion on third down where Joseph missed an open Chris Brooks after extending the play. There were a few questionable decisions on the drive. First was the choice not to continue riding the ground game with the different looks they threw at UCLA. At the very least, Wisconsin needed to get six yards to get into field goal range or get a potential go-for situation on second and third down. Instead, the Badgers punted in plus territory down three. And just like the previous two times, the Bruins made Wisconsin pay, going 89 yards on six plays for their second touchdown of the game. But the waving of the white flag came with five minutes left and the Badgers down 10 points after the defense forced a three-and-out. Once again, Wisconsin couldn’t get anything on their first three downs and faced a 4th & 9 with 4:54 left down two scores. Here, Luke Fickell elected to punt, and the Badgers never got the ball back. After the game, Fickell said he wanted the offense to get into a better situation with six or seven yards to go, but Wisconsin was very likely not getting the ball back twice, let alone once, which is what happened on Saturday. Instead, the Badgers ended the game with their defense on the field as UCLA converted a pair of key third downs and drove down the field again. Third downs Third downs cost Wisconsin the game on both sides of the ball. Wisconsin’s defense, which had been elite at getting off the field on third downs, just could not do so on Saturday. UCLA was 13 of 20 on third downs. And it wasn’t like the Bruins were really getting explosives. Instead, they slowly churned down the field on a number of drives, going 16, 13, 7, 12, 6, and 9 plays on six of their nine drives. They dominated time of possession as a result (37:02 to 22:58), and they especially converted well on their long scoring drives. On their first drive, UCLA converted their first five third downs before failing on the sixth, leading to a field goal in a goal-to-go situation. On their second drive, they went 4 for 4 on third downs. Wisconsin bailed out the Bruins with some penalties, but the Badgers defense could not get off the field, despite stopping the run at a very high level and forcing the Bruins to have an average of 6.1 yards to go on third downs. Wisconsin’s offense on third downs was a worse story. The Badgers were just 3 of 11 on third downs, but the biggest issue was the average distance to go: 9.4 yards. Penalties absolutely killed Wisconsin in this one, and the Badgers constantly found themselves behind the chains on drives where they finally started to have some momentum. It’s near impossible to win when you have to go 9.4 yards on third downs, especially when Wisconsin’s passing offense struggled as much as it did on Saturday, leading to our third takeaway… Struggles in the pass game In every game this season, win or loss, the Badgers have failed to be consistent for four quarters in the passing game. They’ve had their moments and hit on some explosive plays, but it’s been more struggles than successes so far. On Saturday, they couldn’t find any consistency. Colton Joseph completed just 6 of 16 passes for 66 yards, marking the lowest output of a start in his career. Wisconsin had Jaylon Domingeaux back, but it didn’t mean much, as the Badgers got virtually nothing in the air. Wisconsin even had solid protection at times, although UCLA made sure to send extra to force Joseph into poor decisions. The Badgers struggled on the simple concepts, be it inaccurate throws or a dropped pass on a swing pass. And Joseph’s uneven play continued. The quarterback tried to give some of his receivers some opportunities, but he made a couple of questionable decisions once again. Joseph also held the ball too long at times, which has been a common theme this season. Joseph’s legs are the best part of the offense currently, as it opens up the team’s run game to be creative and present different looks as it did for one drive on Saturday. But his struggles in the pass game are well-documented, and UCLA did not give any respect to the aerial attack, loading the box and teeing off with extra rushers. His receivers did not help either. The biggest question in the offseason was whether Wisconsin’s strategy of quantity over getting a clear No. 1 wideout was the right one. Wisconsin’s wideouts have had some quality games this season, but separation, specifically against man coverage, has been an issue. It was never more prevalent than on Saturday against UCLA’s sticky defense. The Badgers wideouts could not generate separation and get open, and the connection on 50/50 balls was not there at all. Joseph did have a nice dime to Malachi Coleman in the end zone near the end of the first half on a should-be touchdown. But Coleman dropped the diving catch, and Wisconsin ended the drive with points after Joseph took a sack on third down and Gavin Lahm missed a 45-yard field goal. Wisconsin had a ton of opportunities on Saturday. Each of their drives, aside from their final one, got to at least their own 40-yard line, with many getting into UCLA territory. Ending with seven points after that is a disappointment.

item.title: Arch Manning reacts after coach does not rule out benching him
item.description: Nov 22, 2025; Austin, Texas, USA; Texas Longhorns quarterback Arch Manning (16) warms up before a game against the Arkansas Razorbacks at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Scott Wachter-Imagn Images Texas Longhorns quarterback Arch Manning entered the season as the favorite to go No. 1 overall in the 2027 NFL Draft. But after another costly turnover in Saturday’s loss to the Florida Gators, his own head coach wouldn’t commit to him as the starter. After the game, Manning responded to Steve Sarkisian’s comments as he embraced the criticism and acknowledged that he needs to perform better. ‘Everything is going to be evaluated’ Texas jumped out to a 17-3 lead over Florida on Saturday, but the Gators scored the next 24 points behind backup quarterback Tramell Jones Jr., who was making his first career start, to pull off a 27-24 upset in Austin. Manning completed 14 of 20 passes for 173 yards and a touchdown, but his late fumble essentially ended the game. That came one week after his late interception helped Oklahoma beat Texas. After the loss, Sarkisian didn’t rule out benching Manning when asked if he would consider a change at quarterback. “We’re not playing good offensive football right now, so everything is going to be evaluated,” Sarkisian said, via On3 . If Texas does decide to make a switch, redshirt freshman K.J. Lacey, a former four-star recruit, would be next in line. ‘That starts with me’ Manning was asked about Sarkisian’s comments after the game, and he didn’t seem bothered by the idea of being evaluated. “Yeah, I mean everyone’s evaluated every week. That’s how it is when you go to a school like this with elite players. Everyone’s gotta get better and that starts with me,” Manning said, via CJ Vogel of On Texas Football. Manning has thrown for more than 250 yards in just one of his last five games and has turned the ball over in crucial moments in back-to-back games. The road doesn’t get much easier for Texas as the team still has to face Ole Miss, Mississippi State, Missouri, and LSU over the next four weeks. Needless to say, Manning will need to back up his words quickly if he wants to hold on to the starting job, because Texas is getting desperate. But the game’s conclusion would not arrive without chaos and controversy. It was ourth and 21 and Florida State, pushed back to the 36-yard line, had only a final heave remaining. Daniels dropped back to near midfield as Miami’s pass rush pressured and unfurled a prayer that for a moment Micahi Danzy appeared to have answered. A two-point conversion attempt to prolong Saturday’s stunner seemed on deck, but a holding penalty on Florida State erased the play and pushed the Seminoles 10 yards further. Daniels again attempted a heave, and again it did not land harmlessly. Robinson and Miami cornerback Bryce Fitzgerald wrestled for the throw as they leaped in the end zone, both grabbing the ball with two hands. But Fitzgerald pulled at it as he fell, holding onto it enough for the referees to call an interception on the field, a ruling that was upheld after review. After a Saturday filled with ranked losses, Miami might find itself as the country’s top-ranked team Sunday. But the Hurricanes were fortunate to not join the crew of national contenders left licking their wounds. Miami’s play was uncharacteristically messy. Defensive back Zechariah Poyser committed an ill-advised targeting penalty in the first quarter that, because of the automatic ejection that comes with the infraction, cost him just about the entirety of the game. Two Hurricane penalties on a second-quarter punt — a facemask and an unsportsmanlike conduct after a fight ensued at midfield — made it awfully easy for Florida State to tie the score at 14 before halftime. Officially, it was a three-play, 15-yard drive that lasted 28 seconds. Miami was marching to start the second half, but quarterback Darian Mensah inexplicably forced a first-down throw toward Barkate, who was blanketed in the end zone, for his first interception of the season. Perhaps the negated Danzy touchdown catch belongs on this list, too. But it’s the victory that counts. A year ago, Miami faltered against Louisville and lost one of two games that nearly derailed its postseason aspirations. This time, they found a way to win. “Credit to our guys because I could sit here and rattle off a million mistakes and errors that we need to correct, but we just kept playing,” Cristobal said. “We just kept battling.” • • • Sign up for our Sports Today newsletter to get daily updates on the Bucs, Rays, Lightning and college football across Florida. item.title: Unlikely 16-year streak continues after Alabama lose to Tennessee
item.description: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Unlikely 16-year streak continues after Alabama lose to Tennessee appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Alabama football ’s struggles continued on Saturday as the Tennessee Volunteers handed the Crimson Tide a disappointing 26-10 loss at Neyland Stadium. Kalen DeBoer’s team suffered another setback in Knoxville, with the loss extending an unwanted streak that dates back 16 years. The Volunteers secured their third consecutive home victory over Alabama in the rivalry. A notable 16-year statistic emerged following the loss, as the last time Alabama lost an away game without fans storming the field was in 2010 against LSU. Crimson Tide quarterback Keelon Russell endured a challenging afternoon against Tennessee’s defense. He completed 19 of his 29 pass attempts for 147 yards but threw two interceptions. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Alabama’s turnover problems proved equally damaging, as the Crimson Tide surrendered possession twice on fumbles in addition to Russell’s interceptions. Tennessee took advantage of those costly mistakes, using the extra opportunities and favorable field position to maintain control of the game. DeBoer was candid when discussing his team’s offensive struggles during the postgame press conference. “Just struggled to sustain anything,” DeBoer said. Keeping drives and continuity there. A penalty or came up short on a couple of fourth downs. You’re going to have to find a way to get some explosives against a front like that. We struggled to do that. Turnovers early, gave them some field position. They got the points.” The defeat leaves Tennessee with a 6-1 overall record and a 3-1 mark in SEC play, while Alabama falls to 5-2 overall and 3-2 in conference competition. The result also marks Alabama’s first consecutive regular-season losses since 2007 after their recent loss against Georgia . Alabama will return to Tuscaloosa next week for its Homecoming matchup against Texas A&M. The Crimson Tide will look to bounce back in front of their home fans and prevent their losing streak from extending to three consecutive games. (Photo by Steve Marcus/Getty Images) Getty Images Sebastian Fundora is incapable of delivering a boring fight. The WBC super welterweight champion successfully defended his title with a 12th-round TKO over Ermal Hadribeaj. The fight wasn’t just a KO in the final round, it was a buzzer-beating shot that appeared to land after the bell. Hadribeaj was hurt and reeling from Fundora’s last-ditch effort to get the stoppage when he went down from a long, straight left hand. Hadribeaj got to his feet before referee Thomas Taylor’s 10 count. However, despite the fight being over, Taylor assessed Hadribeaj and waved off the rest of the count, scoring it a TKO win for Fundora. The reaction to the finish was as spirited as you might expect. item.title: Oh, what a night: Conner Weigman's big game helps UH outlast Oklahoma State in top-20 matchup
item.description: Amare Thomas caught a pair of touchdown passes as UH topped Oklahoma State in a shootout Saturday night at TDECU Stadium. (Jason Fochtman/Houston Chronicle) Conner Weigman threw for 343 yards and five touchdowns, including two to Amare Thomas, to lead No. 20 Houston to a 35-32 win over No. 18 Oklahoma State on Saturday. UH's defense forced two turnovers and made a fourth-down stop near the goal line as the Cougars (6-1, 3-1 Big 12) became bowl eligible with their sixth win and remained in the Big 12 race. Sign up for Cougar Confidential You'll get get in-depth news and analysis about UH's basketball and football teams from reporter Joseph Duarte by signing up for the Cougar Confidential newsletter . After Oklahoma State pulled within 28-25 on a 66-yard touchdown catch-and-run early in the fourth quarter, the Cougars answered as Weigman led an 85-yard drive that took just two minutes. He hooked up with Koby Young on a 48-yard touchdown to push UH's lead to 10. Oklahoma State made one last push, pulling within 35-32 on a 8-yard touchdown catch by Justin Bowick. Mestemaker finished with 365 yards and three touchdowns. Thomas had been quiet the last two games as defenses focused on the All-Big 12 receiver. Thomas set up two key touchdown drives late in the second half, delivering a 51-yard catch-and-spin move to set up Trent Walker's 2-yard touchdown catch. After Oklahoma State scored late in the third quarter, the Cougars were faced with fourth-and-2 at the Cowboys 21. Weigman found Thomas in back right corner of the end zone for a 28-17 lead. Thomas finished with seven catches for 126 yards as UH beat a ranked opponent at home for the first time since a 24-19 win over No. 16 Kansas State in 2024. Oklahoma State (4-2, 2-1 Big 12) managed only a field goal in the first half before Ayo Adeyi scored on a 13-yard run and Drew Mestemaker hit Wyatt Young for a 2-yard TD. Each time the Cowboys scored, UH answered right back. After holding the Cowboys to a field goal on their opening drive, Patrick Overmyer hauled in a 2-yard touchdown, his fifth in the last two games, and Thomas added a 7-yard TD catch for a 14-3 halftime lead. To begin the second half, Oklahoma State marched down the field 75 yards, capped by Adeyi's run to the right side. The drive was aided by a fumble recovery by left tackle Shaun Torgeson. Will James had an interception and had three pass breakups. UH's defense played without three starters - nose guard De'Marion Thomas, linebacker Jaden Yates and cornerback Jalen Mayo. item.title: Here are the five stars from Notre Dame's heartbreaking loss to BYU
item.description: It's tough to give out stars after a loss, but the No. Notre Dame Fighting Irish did have five players worthy of it, even after dropping to No. 8 BYU 28-24. Let's take a look while hoping this nightmare of a Saturday night doesn't hurt the Fighting Irish's playoff chances. You might even see a name or two that you normally don't. Without further adieu, here are tonight's five stars. 5 ⭐️ - Jaden Greathouse Greathouse had eight catches for 125 yards, including what a 38-yarder that kept a potential game-winning drive alive. He appears to be back after being way too quiet as a potential weapon for a very long stretch. 4 ⭐️ - Jordan Faison Faison had a workman-like six catches for 64 yards. 3 ⭐️ - Spencer Porath While touchdowns would've been preferable, Porath's leg helped Irish chip away at BYU's 11-point halftime lead. He put Notre Dame in position to get a lead late. Kicking while facing such a hostile crowd could not have been easy. 2 ⭐️ - Bubba Frazier It didn't lead to a touchdown, only a field goal, but Frazier's recovery of a fumbled punt was huge nonetheless. 1 ⭐️ - Jonaz Walton He had what might've been the game-winning touchdown and a two-point conversion, though his overall numbers looked light, with just 17 yards. That's because he only had five carries. Nolan James Jr. had an OK day with 77 yards on 16 carries, but fans will be clamoring for Walton to start, we bet. A five-stars honorable mention goes out to the Notre Dame fans who were clearly heard chanting "Let's Go Irish!" on the ABC broadcast. A nice effort in an hostile environment. Georgia Bulldogs This week: lost to Auburn 27-24 Next week: Off Who was this version of Gunner Stockton? Whatever it is, the Bulldogs don’t want to see him again! Tennessee Volunteers This week: beat Alabama 26-10 Next week: at South Carolina The Vols had ’em and they smoked ’em (cigars) after beating the arch-rival Crimson Tide. Tennessee’s defense is the real dang deal. Jim Knowles’ crew has given up more than 20 points just once and that was in garbage time during a blowout at Georgia Tech. Tennessee sacked Bama QB Keelon Russell five times and he threw two interceptions. Their win over Oregon State earlier this season looks better by the minute and they’ve beaten their last two Big 12 opponents by a combined 82-32 score. Stein became the first first-year UK coach to start 6-1 since Alpha Brumage in 1913. That’s right — Alpha. item.title: ‘This definitely helped’: Four-star Gaige Weddle on whether BYU could move into his top group
item.description: Gaige Weddle had nothing to say after his experience at BYU on Saturday night. He was too shocked, too excited, too enthralled by what he lived through – a life memory – that the four-star safety from Rancho Bernardo , Calif., did not know how to express himself. “I’m speechless, seriously,” Weddle said. “We all are.” BYU took down Notre Dame in Provo on Saturday night, scored the go-ahead touchdown with less than two minutes left and then had something of a long goal-line stand to stifle the Irish in the closing seconds. ESPN College Gameday was in town. LaVell Edwards Stadium was rocking like maybe never before. After the Cougars held Notre Dame out of the end zone – albeit on a controversial no-call pass interference on the final play – everyone stormed the field in utter jubilation. Weddle was right there to experience it all. “What a sick game,” Weddle said. “Wow. Wow. Wow.” The question now becomes whether this BYU experience moves the needle enough to get the Cougars into the highest group of programs in his recruitment. Trips to UCLA (Oct. 24), Oklahoma (Oct. 31), back to Utah (Nov. 7), Georgia (Nov. 14), Miami (Nov. 21) and Ohio State (Nov. 28) are all coming up. For months, Georgia , Ohio State and Utah have been the three frontrunners with Oklahoma also in that top group. He’s a legacy with the Utes since his father, Eric, starred there before playing for more than a decade in the NFL. He’ll return to Utah in a few weeks. This offseason, Weddle had planned to not take as many visits because he had seen many of his favorites last season. But the four-star rethought that decision and this weekend’s trip to BYU only solidified his belief that getting back on the road was important. But can the Cougars crack that top group after his experience Saturday night? “This definitely helped,” Weddle said.

item.title: Duke under fire after CB swatted away female athletic trainer tending to Landan Callahan’s injury
item.description: Photo by Alex Halloway/Getty Images Duke Blue Devils CB Kimari Robinson is at the centre of a controversy after aggressively swatting away a female athletic trainer who came onto the field to treat teammate Landan Callahan. The Blue Devils lost a rivalry game against the North Carolina Tar Heels 24-20 and might have lost two key defenders over one incident, although only one of the two got injured. After CB Landan Callahan went down with an injury, leading to a concerned Kimari Robinson hovering over him, Robinson made a huge mistake by swatting away a female athletic trainer who came to work on Callahan. Kimari Robinson under extreme scrutiny after swatting away a female athletic trainer After Callahan went down in the third quarter, Robinson had his moment with trainer Grace Dietrich, prompting a lot of angry fans to criticise his behaviour. “The kid needs to be benched for a game or two, and forced to go through the emergency training again. You can’t have someone that big and strong, acting like that in an emergency. Imagine if he had accidentally connected and floored her, giving her a concussion? Suddenly he’d be up on assault charges, and there would be a second medical emergency distracting the medics trying to help his teammate,” said a fan . “He’s a punk, and Duke better make sure he learns a lesson from this,” said another angry fan . “Unacceptable, I have to let the medical staff do what they need to do,” said one fan . “Player should not be there. Let the medical staff do their job. They clearly suspect a neck injury, as the ATC is immobilising the head. She is clearly just trying to make room to do her job,” said another fan who was angry at the player . “I get your point, but the emotions of a kid when someone as close as family is hurting and down isn’t a thing to dismiss either. They both obviously care for the down player,” said one fan in defence of the player . With some calling for consequences like missing games for Robinson, the Blue Devils will be left in a tough spot. While they have to discipline the 21-year-old, they also need him on the field after a 1-2 start to the season. Robinson has five tackles in two games for the Blue Devils as a starting CB, registering three against the Tar Heels. item.title: Oklahoma’s John Mateer throws away another game with brutal interception
item.description: Oklahoma’s John Mateer (10) warms up before the college football game between the University of Oklahoma Sooners (OU) and the Kentucky Wildcats at Gaylord Family — Oklahoma Memorial Stadium in Norman, Okla., Saturday, Oct., 17, 2026. Oklahoma’s John Mateer throws away another game with brutal interception appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Oklahoma football welcomed the Kentucky Wildcats to Norman, Oklahoma in a sneaky-tough game that came after coach Brent Venables was patted on the back for his win over Texas. Oklahoma legend Gerald McCoy was among those trolling the Longhorns after the Sooners’ big win, but the tables turned against Kentucky as quarterback John Mateer made another egregious error. Mateer’s Sooners trailed by one point with 1:25 left on the clock on their side of the field. Mateer took a deep drop, looked over the middle and threw it late into double coverage as Jordan Castell made an interception that he returned for a touchdown, extending the Wildcats’ late lead to 21-13. John Mateer throws a back-breaking pick-six to help Kentucky pull away from Oklahoma late in the fourth quarter. pic.twitter.com/VpXnSt3qoJ Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) — Underdog CFB (@UnderdogCFB) October 18, 2026 The Wildcats held on for a 21-13 victory in hostile territory, sending Mateer and Venables’ team to 3-3 and likely ending their College Football Playoff hopes. It was a bitter pill for Mateer and the Sooners to swallow, one week after their biggest win of the season. Kentucky scored 14 fourth quarter points to steal the win, shocking the Vegas oddsmakers on a day when they recorded less than 250 yards. Mateer, who’s been blasted by Skip Bayless for his recent mistakes , ended up with 270 yards passing and a touchdown, but three interceptions continued his startling trend of being careless with the football in the worst possible moments. The Sooners got nearly 200 yards rushing combined from Isaiah Sategna III and Manny Choice, but couldn’t cash in with points. Mateer’s job seemed safe after the Texas upset, but now appears on shaky ground once again as the Sooners will look to turn the page against Mississippi State in Week 8. item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.description: A match delayed by missile attack warnings is not what Cristiano Ronaldo and co signed up for but it’s the new reality; the Saudi sporting juggernaut is stalling Cristiano Ronaldo grabbed the scarf in the colours of the Saudi Arabian flag and waved it at the sparse but enthusiastic crowd, who responded with rapturous cheers. It was a gesture of defiance rather than a victory salute, encapsulating the Saudi equivalent of “Keep calm and carry on”. Monday night’s Asian Champions League Elite game between Al-Nassr and the Uzbek side Neftchi Fergana had ended with a 3-1 win for the Saudi club coached by Ange Postecoglou, with Ronaldo, supported by Sadio Mané, scoring, the smattering of star names indicative of the lure of the Saudi Pro League. Yet this isn’t quite how Ronaldo and co would have anticipated life in Riyadh. The meagre attendance aside, Monday’s game was delayed by a threat of missile attacks from Yemen’s Houthi rebels. A safety warning issued 15 minutes before kick-off came two days after 13 people died and more than 300 were wounded by Houthi strikes on Riyadh’s King Khalid international airport. item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Do Premier League teams really need to run more to win matches?
item.description: Pundits regularly criticise teams for not running enough but is there a link between distance covered and results? By Opta Analyst It was like clockwork. Manchester United dropped points against Tottenham and critics were quick to question their effort and application, using the team’s physical statistics to make points. Speaking on Sky Sports, Jamie Redknapp said: “There’s a pattern I don’t really like when I watch teams, and that’s when – and the stats don’t lie – the other team runs more than you. In the Premier League right now, I feel there are a couple of non-negotiables: you’ve got to run more than the other team if you want to win, or at least get close enough that it doesn’t make that much of a difference. Tottenham ran five kilometres more than Manchester United.” Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Guardiola returns to Manchester as City spin into dizzy mess against PSG
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! It is quite funny that PSG felt like the good guys at the Etihad Stadium but if we briefly detach ourselves from the notion that the European champions’ own sportswashing and cashsplashing has also done immeasurable damage to the beautiful game, then their 4-2 Bigger Cup shellacking of Manchester City was pure cinema, baby! I was stunned at reading the comments in support of Manchester City keeping their trophies, coming out of the mouth of their Bigger Cup rivals at PSG (yesterday’s Quote of the Day). Given the example of the organisers of the Tour de Lance … sorry, the Tour de France, this kind of ‘keep the awards you won’ stuff might get him sent to the Bastille. Or consider Formula One. They’ve got all kinds of rules about driver behaviour on the racetrack, and additional rules about what the crew can and cannot do to your car. Cars get inspected before each race, and there are also mandatory post-race inspections for every car. You might drive your car first across the line to the cheers of the crowd, but if the post-race inspection discovered that you cheated in how your team designed your vehicle, your memory of crossing the line is all you get to keep. Think about that for a minute. If the Premier League and Fifa cannot clear the bar for morals in sport set by the UCI and FIA, that says a lot. And none of it good” – Peter Rehwaldt. My friend Bernard grew up in Coventry. And as a boy he thought the team was called ‘Coventry City Nil’. I would get out more, but I’m a Manchester United fan” – Brendan Hughes. item.description: A famous name and record attendances have given FCK a platform but a difficult start in Denmark’s top-flight shows success on the pitch is not guaranteed On an August day in 2024, 5,165 fans gathered at Vanløse Idrætspark to watch FC Copenhagen (FCK) take on B73 Slagelse in their first league match. For Denmark’s most successful men’s club, with 16 league titles, it marked the realisation of their desire to establish a women’s team, through collaboration with the existing FC Damsø, and an ambitious project with aims of having a wide-reaching impact on and off the pitch. The 26 months since have brought a whirlwind of success, the club securing back-to-back promotions to reach the A-Liga. Now they are in the top division and “playing with the big dogs”, as their head of women’s football, Romaney Pinnock, coins it, and they must adapt to stay there. Continue reading...

item.title: Hong Kong club hope David Silva can be their hero – but just for one day
item.description: Former Manchester City player is coming out of retirement at 40 to play one match for ambitious Supreme Sha Tin Hong Kong, China (as is the official football name), has long tried to follow the advice of Han Solo in Return of the Jedi: keeping their distance from China while trying not to look like they are keeping their distance. It is all about maintaining an independent football association and the trappings and privilege that come with it. There was some talk a few years ago about getting a Hong Kong team in the Chinese Super League, when the spending was in full flow, and although that did not happen the local Premier League has belatedly got in on the act – kind of. This glittering city is not known as a football hotbed but has a long history in the sport that started when it was a British colony and has continued since it became a special administrative region of China in 1997. George Best, Peter Shilton, Arie Haan, Bobby Moore, Diego Forlán, Nicky Butt, René van de Kerkhof, Tony Morley, Gordon McQueen and Craig Foster have played in the territory and soon David Silva will too. item.description: It’s not just that the club’s recent charges themselves are unprecedented – it’s the language used to describe them too Sign up for our free newsletter here The language of football is a fine and highly nuanced dialect. The majority of people involved in the game speak it with a high degree of sophistication. Minor deviations from the familiar, almost imperceptible to outsiders, can set off alarm bells: what’s really going on there? Why isn’t he happy? What’s she hinting at? But it’s an argot developed to talk about football, and when applied to other subjects, it can sound extremely jarring. Erling Haaland is one of the brighter, more engaging players. There’s an appealing quirkiness to him that suggests he has a higher-than-usual level of self-awareness. He doesn’t mind stepping outside the norms, being a bit different. item.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action
item.description: Manchester City unrepentant in victory, Spurs make progress of a sort and Noni Madueke meets the moment The manner of Manchester City’s victory at Liverpool was an article of both vindication and vilification. Those gleefully wielding inflatable bananas in the Anfield away end could thumb their noses. Why not enjoy the dances of defiance until the music stops? The same went for City players, asked to perform under the darkest of clouds, able to focus, at last, on football, rather than legal argument and uncertain futures. Beyond City, the sight of a club found guilty of 100-plus charges laying waste to such rivals as Liverpool was deeply uncomfortable . The Premier League season and product are badly damaged until the matter is somehow resolved. What happened at Anfield should double the haste for a resolution. Chants of “cheat” whenever City players, the game already won, slipped the ball around, are bound to be repeated at other stadiums. Enzo Maresca has described his club’s plight as “noise” but his team’s victory did absolutely nothing to turn the volume down. item.title: Why we’re stuck with a Premier League in the clutches of the global mega-rich | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s little prospect of the model changing in a country that welcomes wealthy international owners with open arms Football, the world’s most popular sport, played by laws drawn up in London in 1863. The Premier League is the UK’s greatest soft power export. Premier League clubs are owned by a deputy prime minister of Abu Dhabi, the public investment fund of Saudi Arabia, a billionaire based in Monaco for tax reasons and a disappointing assortment of investors and private equity funds. And what, really, could be more British than that? Football truly is the national game. What the Manchester City case has exposed is just how difficult it is to regulate some of the richest and most powerful bodies in the world. While the wait for the verdict was frustrating, it was perhaps unavoidable given the possibility of legal objection at every turn when a leaked email from City’s in-house lawyer during Uefa’s action against the club had threatened to “ spend 30 million on the 50 best lawyers in the world to sue them for the next 10 years”. You didn’t get that with Albert Alexander Sr or Peter Swales. Continue reading...

Kai Havertz, David Raya and Mikel Merino, who issues commands in Spanish and has spoken about spending time with Win when out for three months with a foot injury, are particular favourites. But, according to sources close to Win, a therapy dog trained not to bark, there is no contest when it comes to her preferred human: Arteta. Continue reading...

That ambition was fulfilled during a brilliant international career that ended this week “What Argentina is doing in this World Cup is of a sacred order,” Brazilian writer Milly Lacombe posted at the height of the tide of anti-Argentinian sentiment during this year’s tournament. She was exploring the contradiction she felt around her support of Lionel Messi: “a player who is a God and a man who shakes Trump’s hand”. Lacombe highlighted the importance of acknowledging the complexities around Messi and the Argentinian team. How is it possible that Messi was not speaking out against the racist incidents we all saw around the Argentina team , she asked. “That’s why it hurts so much to see someone with Messi’s power choosing to make himself small,” she wrote. item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
